screening.reason: Meets inclusion 2/3: analyses ABIDE I resting-state fMRI functional connectivity for both group-difference (over/under-connectivity) and SVM diagnostic classification.

evidence_spans.text:
we selected a 
subgroup of 190 subjects (102 with ASD and 88 TD) according to the following criteria: male 
children (age range: 6.5–13 years); rs-fMRI data acquired with open eyes; data from the 
University sites that provided the largest number of scans (KKI, NYU, UCLA, UM).
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort was a 190-subject (102 ASD, 88 TD) subset of ABIDE I selected by age, sex, eye status and site.

evidence_spans.text:
We analyzed the preprocessed data available on the ABIDE 
preprocessed homepage (29, 30), using the Configurable Pipeline 
for the Analysis of Connectomes (CPAC) (31), that includes slice-
timing, motion correction, intensity normalization, nuisance 
signal removal (e.g. tissue signals, low-frequency drifts), and 
registrations.
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing used the Preprocessed Connectomes Project CPAC pipeline.

evidence_spans.text:
Both anatomical and functional atlases were chosen to derive the 
FC measures; in particular, we chose Harvard-Oxford (HO) and 
Automatic Anatomical Labeling (AAL) as anatomical templates 
and Craddock-200 (CC) as functional templates to extract time 
series from brain regions
evidence_spans.claim: Four atlases (AAL, HO, CC, Power) were compared for the connectivity analysis.

evidence_spans.text:
a leave-site out cross-validation scheme was performed: 
each training set was composed by all the sites except one, that 
was left out for validation.
evidence_spans.claim: Classification used a leave-one-site-out cross-validation scheme.

evidence_spans.text:
The mean L-SVM classification performance, 
in terms of the area under the ROC curve (AUC), was 0.75 ± 0.05. The highest performance 
was obtained using data from KKI, NYU and UCLA sites in training and data from UM as testing 
set (AUC = 0.83).
evidence_spans.claim: Leave-one-site-out SVM classification reached mean AUC 0.75 ± 0.05, best fold AUC 0.83.

evidence_spans.text:
Specifically, stronger functional connectivity (FC) in ASD with respect to TD 
involve (p < 0.001) the angular gyrus with the precuneus in the right (R) hemisphere, and the 
R frontal operculum cortex with the pars opercularis of the left (L) inferior frontal gyrus.
evidence_spans.claim: ASD showed hyper-connectivity between right angular gyrus-precuneus (DMN) and right frontal operculum-left IFG pars opercularis.

evidence_spans.text:
implementation of the HO atlas. The binary classification 
results between subjects with ASD and controls in a leave-one-
site-out cross-validation scheme achieved an average accuracy 
of 0.71 ± 0.06 and an average AUC of 0.75  ± 0.05.
evidence_spans.claim: Best atlas (HO) gave leave-one-site-out accuracy 0.71 ± 0.06 and AUC 0.75 ± 0.05.

evidence_spans.text:
DATA AVAILABILITY
Publicly available datasets were analyzed in this study. This data 
can be found here: http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/
evidence_spans.claim: Data availability statement points only to the general ABIDE repository, not a specific participant list for this subsample.

assessments.support: Explicit, stepwise selection criteria (age 6.5-13, male, eyes open, four most-populated sites) with resulting N by diagnosis given: "we selected a subgroup of 190 subjects (102 with ASD and 88 TD) according to the following criteria"
Named pipeline (CPAC) and four named atlases (AAL, HO, CC, Power) with feature counts per atlas reported in Table 4.
ASD/TD diagnosis is the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis (DSM-5-based, ADOS Gotham scores reported), independent of the imaging predictor.

Leave-one-site-out cross-validation used throughout, whole-brain features without a tuned feature-selection step, and fixed default SVM hyperparameter to avoid a leakage-prone nested search: "a leave-site out cross-validation scheme was performed: each training set was composed by all the sites except one, that was left out for validation."

risk_of_bias.summary: Well-documented cohort-definition, pipeline, atlas choice and leave-one-site-out evaluation with no evident leakage; the main limitation is that only four of the larger ABIDE I sites are used and no held-out replication cohort is reported.

charting.feature_extraction_tools: Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (CPAC), via the ABIDE Preprocessed Connectomes Project
charting.specific_features: Pearson-correlation (Fisher z-transformed) functional connectivity using AAL, Harvard-Oxford (HO), Craddock-200 (CC) and Power atlases
charting.specific_algorithms: Linear SVM classification, compared across AAL/HO/CC/Power parcellations
charting.validation_methodology: Leave-one-site-out cross-validation across KKI, NYU, UCLA, UM
charting.key_performance_results: Best atlas (HO): mean leave-one-site-out AUC 0.75 ± 0.05, accuracy 0.71 ± 0.06; best fold (train KKI/NYU/UCLA, test UM) AUC 0.83
charting.features_associated_disorder: Stronger (hyper-) connectivity in ASD between right angular gyrus and right precuneus (DMN), and between right frontal operculum and left IFG pars opercularis; weaker (hypo-) connections also reported (e.g. intra-hemispheric right temporal fusiform)
charting.feature_change_direction: Mixed hyper- and hypo-connectivity, varying by connection
charting.dataset_openly_available: No study-specific participant list or code; only the general ABIDE repository link is given

items.support: Explicit stepwise selection criteria and resulting N by diagnosis.
Motion correction named as a pipeline step but no subject-level motion threshold given.
CPAC pipeline and processing strategies named.
ASD/TD is the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis; ADOS Gotham total/severity scores reported per site.
No tuned feature selection (reduces leakage risk) but no explicit leakage-control statement.
No study-specific participant list or code; only the general ABIDE link given.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Both (group-difference + diagnostic prediction); ABIDE I subset of 190 male children (102 ASD, 88 TD), ages 6.5-13, from KKI, NYU, UCLA and UM.
narrative_row.methods: CPAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; functional connectivity under AAL, HO, CC and Power atlases; permutation testing for group differences; linear-SVM classification with leave-one-site-out cross-validation.
narrative_row.outcomes: Best atlas (HO): leave-one-site-out mean AUC 0.75±0.05, accuracy 0.71±0.06, best fold AUC 0.83; hyper-connectivity in ASD between right angular gyrus-precuneus and right frontal operculum-left IFG, plus weaker connections elsewhere.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Restricted to male children at four sites; no study-specific participant list published; feature selection not attempted so no leakage-control procedure was needed or described in detail.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A methodologically thorough ABIDE I subset analysis combining connectivity group-difference findings with a properly site-cross-validated SVM classifier; selection rule is exact enough to approximate reconstruction but no ID list is given.
